breaking_changes.BC_description: The Promise.using method has been removed. It was used for resource management with disposers.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Use Promise.try or manual resource management instead. Example: Before - Promise.using(getResource(), disposer => { /* code */ }); After - const resource = getResource(); Promise.try(() => { /* code */ }).finally(() => disposer(resource));

breaking_changes.BC_description: The Promise.settle method has been removed. It was used to wait for all promises to settle, regardless of fulfillment or rejection.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Use Promise.allSettled (native or polyfilled) or implement custom logic. Example: Before - Promise.settle([promise1, promise2]); After - Promise.allSettled([promise1, promise2]);

breaking_changes.BC_description: The Promise.prototype.progress method has been removed. It was used for handling progress events in promises.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Use event emitters or custom progress handling. Example: Before - promise.progress(handler); After - Implement progress events manually, e.g., using EventEmitter or callbacks.

breaking_changes.BC_description: The Promise.prototype.done method has been removed. It was used to handle promise resolution without returning a promise.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Use .then or .catch for handling, and ensure to handle errors to prevent unhandled rejections. Example: Before - promise.done(onFulfilled, onRejected); After - promise.then(onFulfilled).catch(onRejected);

breaking_changes.BC_description: The Promise.longStackTraces configuration has been removed. It was used to enable long stack traces for better debugging.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Use native stack traces or alternative debugging tools. There is no direct replacement; adjust debugging practices accordingly.

breaking_changes.BC_description: The Promise.onPossiblyUnhandledRejection and Promise.onUnhandledRejectionHandled methods have been removed. They were used for global rejection handling.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Use process.on('unhandledRejection', handler) in Node.js or window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', handler) in browsers for global rejection handling. Example: Before - Promise.onPossiblyUnhandledRejection(handler); After - process.on('unhandledRejection', handler);

breaking_changes.BC_description: The Promise.fromNode method has been renamed to Promise.fromCallback. It was used to convert Node.js-style callbacks to promises.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Replace all instances of Promise.fromNode with Promise.fromCallback. Example: Before - Promise.fromNode(callback); After - Promise.fromCallback(callback);

breaking_changes.BC_description: The Promise.prototype.timeout method now throws a Promise.TimeoutError instead of a generic Error when a promise times out.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Update error handling to catch Promise.TimeoutError specifically. Example: Before - promise.timeout(1000).catch(error => { if (error.message.includes('timeout')) { /* handle timeout */ } }); After - promise.timeout(1000).catch(error => { if (error instanceof Promise.TimeoutError) { /* handle timeout */ } });

breaking_changes.BC_description: The Promise.config method has been removed. It was used to configure global promise settings.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: There is no direct replacement; remove all calls to Promise.config and rely on default settings or alternative configuration methods if available.

breaking_changes.BC_description: The Promise.prototype.nodeify method has been removed. It was used to convert a promise to a Node.js-style callback.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Manually handle callbacks using .then and .catch. Example: Before - promise.nodeify(callback); After - promise.then(value => callback(null, value)).catch(error => callback(error));

breaking_changes.BC_description: Cancellation has been redesigned in bluebird 3.0, making any code relying on 2.x cancellation semantics incompatible.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Refer to the Cancellation documentation for new semantics. No direct adaptation provided; requires review and update of cancellation-related code.
breaking_changes.RequireInfo: Comprehensive details on the specific changes to cancellation semantics and examples of how to adapt existing code are needed.

breaking_changes.BC_description: Promise.promisify's second argument is now an options object instead of a context, breaking code that used the old signature.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Change the second argument from context to an options object with a context property. Example: Before - Promise.promisify(fn, ctx); After - Promise.promisify(fn, {context: ctx});

breaking_changes.BC_description: Promise.promisify, Promise.promisifyAll, and Promise.fromCallback now ignore multiple callback arguments by default, resolving only with the first argument, unlike 2.x which used an array for multiple arguments.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Use the multiArgs option set to true to preserve the old behavior of resolving with an array of arguments. Example: Before - No option needed; After - Promise.promisify(fn, {multiArgs: true});

breaking_changes.BC_description: Promise.each and .each no longer return the original array; they now return a new array with values from the iterator callback, similar to Promise.map.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: If the original array was needed, store it separately before calling .each. Example: Before - const result = promise.each(iterator); // result is original array; After - const originalArray = array; promise.each(iterator).then(newArray => { /* use newArray or originalArray as needed */ });

breaking_changes.BC_description: Promise progression has been completely removed, breaking any code that used progress handlers.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Use alternative methods for progress handling, such as event emitters or custom callbacks. No direct replacement; implement manually.

breaking_changes.BC_description: .spread's second argument has been removed, breaking code that relied on it.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Remove the second argument and handle the spread values differently if needed. Example: Before - promise.spread((arg1, arg2) => { /* code */ }, handler); After - promise.spread((arg1, arg2) => { /* code */ }); // handler must be integrated elsewhere if necessary.
breaking_changes.RequireInfo: Clarification on what the second argument was used for and specific examples of adaptation are needed.

breaking_changes.BC_description: .done now causes an irrecoverable fatal error in Node.js environments, breaking code that used it for handling.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Replace .done with .then and .catch to handle promise resolution and errors properly. Example: Before - promise.done(onFulfilled, onRejected); After - promise.then(onFulfilled).catch(onRejected);

breaking_changes.BC_description: Errors from Promise.reject or the reject callback are no longer marked as OperationalErrors, which may affect error handling logic.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Update error handling code to not rely on OperationalError marking. Check error properties directly if needed.

breaking_changes.BC_description: The .progress method of PromiseResolver has been removed, breaking code that used it for progressing promises.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Use alternative methods for progress handling, such as event emitters or custom callbacks. No direct replacement; implement manually.
